ruleName: Player out of bounds but ball on the course
group: Player out of bounds but ball on the course
imagePrompt: A teenage boy golfer is about to play his ball, which sits inside the white out of bounds line. He moves a rubbish bin just outside the line to clear space for his stance.
imageAlt: Boy golfer moving a rubbish bin located just outside the white out of bounds line as he prepares to hit a ball inside the line.

issues: The iron is grounded rather than in the golfer's hands at the moment, but this is contextually understandable given the bin movement action.
imageVerification.repairPrompt: Show the teenage golfer holding the iron club naturally in one hand while moving the rubbish bin, ensuring the club is not left grounded. Otherwise, maintain all current details.

questions.title: Moving things like bins that are out of bounds
questions.question: If there is something you can move, like a rubbish bin, and it is out of bounds but is in your way when you stand to hit your ball that is on the course, can you move it?

choices.text: Yes, you can move things you are allowed to move, even if they are out of bounds.
No, you cannot move anything that is out of bounds.
Yes, but only if the bin is partly on the course.
No, you have to play with it in the way.

questions.explanation: You can move things like bins, even if they are out of bounds, if they get in your way when you hit your ball from the course.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: An area outside the edge of the course where you can't play your ball.
Something you are allowed to move, like a bin, a branch, or a bottle.

questions.teachingTip: Show the difference between things you can move (like a bin or bottle) and things that can't be moved (like trees or fences). Ask kids to spot movable obstructions on the course.
likelyMisconceptions: Kids may think you can’t move anything that is out of bounds.
Some may think you have to play around it even if it is not on the course.

questions.title: Relief from movable obstructions outside the course
questions.question: If a movable obstruction, like a rubbish bin, is out of bounds but interferes with your stance when you play your ball on the course, can you move it?

choices.text: Yes, you can move movable obstructions even if they're out of bounds.
No, you cannot move anything that is located out of bounds.
Yes, but only if the bin is partly in bounds.
No, you must play around it.

questions.explanation: You are allowed to move moveable obstructions, even when they are out of bounds, if they affect your stroke at a ball on the course.
